a_stored_transmural_vector: n = f x s of data/biv/<H>/fibres_v51/bivF_v51.lon (the .lon holds the fibre f and the sheet s; s is the in-wall cross-fibre column, so the transmural direction is the sheet normal). For LV-side elements fibres_fix.py built it as column e2 of its frame: grad phi_lv, grad phi_rv and grad phi_epi_fix, each orthogonalised to l, bislerped by d and by phi_epi_fix, so yes, from transmural gradients (rotated with the fibre about e2, which leaves e2 unchanged)
